1.

Wilt thou not hearken to love’s entreaty, Cease to live unto thyself at pleasure, Far from the God who hath seen how thou hast wandered, A stranger to Him day after day?

2.

Feelest thou not how long thou hast erred, And how thou hast ever despised His goodness? Yet still resounds the gracious message, Which many a time already thine ear hath reached.

3.

O, how He longeth to set thee free, To lift off the burden of sins so heavy! In His tenderness He will now enfold thee In a love that eternally is young.

4.

No reproach, no anger Meeteth thee, for He took the judgment upon Himself! All God’s righteousness’ holy demand He fulfilled here on the cross for thee.

5.

And when thy journey here below is ended, Thou shalt before Christ above stand forth As an eternal witness of His victory, The victory His love once for us won.
